name: Demolition contractor

pf.license.need: if: a contractor or demolition registration or license for the company, where the state's form requires one (often by job size or kind of work)
ask: The company's registration or license number, and its class
Any job-size limit the license has
General liability insurance; workers' comp where the business has employees
A bond, where the state's form asks for one
pf.license.holder: The business; plus a qualifying person where the state's form names one. Trade subcontractors (asbestos and lead removal, utility capping, trucking and hauling) hold their own, as the state's form requires.
pf.license.check: none: Rosie never looks up, checks or confirms a license, insurance or registration (D96); anything shown is as given by the business, not checked by Rosie
blocks: No demolition work goes live until the company's registration or license checks out, where one is required
A job over the license's size limit is never offered or quoted: the owner is told why
pf.license.renewals: License, insurance and bond dates kept; reminded 30 days out; a lapse pauses new bookings
pf.license.lead_safe: Work that disturbs paint in older buildings only by a firm and a person certified for lead-safe work, where the rules require it. Asbestos is removed only by a licensed removal company, never by this crew
pf.license.design_studio: A consult at the office needs no license in most states. The work it leads to is booked under the contractor license.
pf.license.background: Background checks only where the state's form asks

pf.services.pattern: Estimate visit, then project: the job is booked only after a written quote and a signed contract

B.name: Estimate visit
B.price: $89, credited to the job if Alex signs (the example business's own price; a free estimate is a starting option)
B.before: nothing taken (or a card saved for the $89)
B.after: billed only if no contract follows

B.name: Garage or shed teardown
B.price: quoted after the estimate visit by size and materials: a written quote within 3 business days, good for 30 days
B.length: about 2 to 4 work days, with a haul-off
B.before: nothing at booking; a deposit only after the contract is signed
B.after: stage bills as each checked stage is done; the last after the site is cleared

B.name: Interior demolition (kitchen or bath gut, non-load-bearing walls)
Wall removal
B.price: quoted after the estimate visit; a wall that holds up a roof or a floor needs an engineer's letter from the owner first

B.name: Concrete, patio, deck or pool removal
Whole-building demolition (large; only inside the license's size limit)
B.price: quoted after the estimate visit; the survey, utility shut-offs, permit and neighbor notices come first

B.name: Shed teardown
B.price: priced from photos (example: $640); over $500, Sam OKs it
B.before: a signed contract, then a 25% deposit

B.name: Cleanout help
B.price: $179, from the list (2 workers, up to 1 hour); a repeat plan is possible
B.where: at the customer's place; nobody needs to be home
B.before: a card saved for the $89 fee

B.name: Debris pickup
B.price: $150, from the list (one truck load); also a yearly plan

B.name: Pre-demolition site check
B.before: a card saved for the $89 fee

B.name: Change order
B.price: priced, written and signed by both before the changed work; added to the next stage bill

B.name: Permit, survey, utility shut-offs, dumpster and disposal fees
B.price: in every quote; asbestos or lead removal is a licensed company's own quote

A.name: Scope consult
A.where: at the office, or by video or phone; or at the customer's home for $75, paid in full when booked
A.before: a card saved for the $20 missed-consult fee

A.name: Teardown phasing session
A.price: $55, 60 minutes; credited to the job if Alex signs

A.name: Demolition planning package (scope, permit list, disposal plan)
A.before: a $40 deposit; the $100 rest at the office desk

A.name: Custom scope sheet
A.price: priced from the customer's photos and measurements (example: $90); Sam OKs each one

A.name: Scope revision
A.price: priced at the office after a $25 consult

pf.services.capacity: One estimator or planner per booking; one demolition crew per job at a time; the office's table is saved with long sessions
pf.services.skills: Estimates and running a job: crew leads. Scope consults: planners. Asbestos and lead removal, utility capping and hauling: licensed subcontractors.
pf.services.nobody_home: Estimates, cleanouts and pickups: nobody needs to be home if the gate is open. Teardown days: the building must be empty, and an adult on the booking is reachable by phone.
pf.services.online: A scope consult can be a video or phone call (counts as at the office)
pf.services.smallest_job: A switch the owner sets: the smallest job taken, with smaller requests pointed elsewhere (the example takes no teardown under 80 square feet; smaller jobs are cleanouts).

before_times: What do you want taken down or hauled off? (a garage, a shed, a wall, a slab, a deck, a cleanout)
Rough size, length by width, or just a guess
The year the building was built (older buildings may need an asbestos and lead test first, where the rules require it)
after_time: Who will sign the contract? Everyone on the deed should be at the estimate visit
Do you own the property or rent? (the owner must sign)
Is anyone living in or using the building? It must be empty before any teardown
Are the power, gas, water and sewer still connected there?
Where can a dumpster or truck stand? Gates, low wires, a narrow street
A well, a septic tank, an oil tank or sprinkler lines near the work
pf.questions.who_may_book: An adult who owns the property, or someone with the owner's written OK. A renter's or a neighbor's job needs the owner to sign. A building that someone lives in is never booked for a teardown.
studio: Which area, and a rough budget (on the secure page)

stop.words: gas smell, hissing near a gas line, sparking or smoking wires, a carbon monoxide alarm
stop.says: Leave the building now. Then call 911 and the gas or power company.
stop.booking: no booking; a new request must say the building was made safe

stop.words: a wall, roof or floor falling or collapsing now, or someone trapped or hurt in a building
stop.says: Get everyone out and away from the building, and call 911.

steps_then_go_on.words: a fire- or storm-damaged building that is still standing, with nobody inside
steps_then_go_on.says: Stay out of it and keep children and pets away. The crew lead looks at it from outside first.

steps_then_go_on.words: worry about asbestos or lead dust in an old building
steps_then_go_on.says: Don't break, sand or scrape old floors, pipes, plaster or paint. We'll test first.
steps_then_go_on.booking: goes on; testing becomes a first step

pf.safety.business_line: Questions about whether a wall holds up the roof or a floor, or about a neighbor's wall, go to the business's own line

pf.first_steps.before_quote: The estimate visit at the property, with everyone who will sign there
after_contract: The cancel window ends before any work or orders, where the state's rules give one
The survey: older buildings are tested for asbestos and lead before any teardown, where the rules require it, and the start waits for the result
The utilities: power, gas, water and sewer shut off and capped, and confirmed by the utility before the first work day
The permit, pulled by the license holder in the business's name, where the work needs one
The dumpster spot, and the neighbor notice where the rules require it
prep: Empty the building of anything you want to keep, and keep people and pets out of it
Move cars, planters and fences away from the work area and the truck path
Mark sprinkler heads and lines you know about
Keep children and pets away from the site
Put any gate or lockbox code on the secure page
studio_prep: Bring photos and rough measurements of the area
Bring any samples or colors you already like

pf.visit.check_in: Estimate visit: the check-in code at the door. Each work day: that day's code, or the lockbox and a start photo when nobody is home. Office: the code at the desk.
pf.visit.at_the_visit: The estimator walks the building, checks what is inside and what is still connected (power, gas, water, sewer), measures and photographs; the written quote follows within 3 business days, good for 30 days
pf.visit.changes: A written change order, priced and signed by both, before any changed work. A hidden second layer, an unmarked line or extra hauling is priced this way.
pf.visit.outside_checks: The survey result before the start, the utilities' confirmations, and a final check or permit sign-off, where the rules require them
pf.visit.done: The site cleared and graded as the contract says, the final check where needed, the walk-through, then DONE on the last work day; the care notes go with it
pf.visit.studio_done: DONE after the consult, with the planner's notes and the picks saved for the estimate
pf.visit.before_photos: The building and the lot, the fence line, the curb and the driveway, and anything nearby that could be hit

pf.money.estimate: The example's $89 estimate visit is credited to the job; billed only if no contract follows. A free estimate is the safe start.
pf.money.no_money_before_contract: On project work, nothing is taken before the contract is signed by everyone on the deed
pf.money.deposit: Only after signing; the deposit cap comes from the state's form
pf.money.kept_apart: Money paid before the work is kept apart or bonded where the state's rules require it (a switch from the state's form)
pf.money.stages: Each stage is billed only when it's done and any check has passed: the start, the teardown and haul-off, the finish. Never ahead of the work
pf.money.last_payment: After the site is cleared and the final check passes
pf.money.change_orders: Added to the next stage bill
pf.money.big_bills: Bank transfer through the company's own Stripe, for bills over the owner's amount (the example: $500); paid once it clears. A check also works: the crew lead texts 'paid check'.
pf.money.tax: Tax on materials and labor follows the state's form
pf.money.studio: The teardown phasing session's $55 is credited to the job if Alex signs; the $20 missed-consult fee only after Sam OKs it

never_in_texts: Contract, change order and permit papers (secure page only, with a copy by email)
pf.messages.minors: Never booked by a minor; a child at home is never the one who lets the crew in

pf.staff.roles: Crew leads (Walt, Cruz): estimates, quotes and running the job, with the crew. Planners (Fern, Asa) at the office.
pf.staff.licenses: The company holds the contractor registration or license. Where the state's form also licenses each person, each one may add a number (optional, shown as given, not checked by Rosie). Subcontractors hold their own, as the business says.
pf.staff.lead_safe: A certified renovator on each job in an older building, where lead-safe rules apply
pf.staff.who_oks: Sam OKs quotes and change orders over $500; Pat may OK them too, and Sam's answer wins
pf.staff.stand_in: Another crew lead may take an estimate visit; a job keeps its crew lead unless Sam moves it

pf.rules.contract: A written contract for project work where the state's rules require one, signed by everyone on the deed and by the business before any money
pf.rules.contract_parts: The parts the state's form lists (license number, dates, price, deposit, cancel notice, any lien notice)
pf.rules.cancel_window: A cancel window after signing, where the state's rules give one; work and orders wait for it
pf.rules.permits: Pulled by the license holder in the business's name, never the homeowner's
pf.rules.change_orders: Written and signed by both before the changed work
pf.rules.final: The final check and any permit sign-off before the last payment
pf.rules.lien_waivers: Lien waivers from the business and its subcontractors with the last payment, where the state's rules provide them
pf.rules.show: The license number on the listing, the quote, the contract and the receipt, where the state's rules require it
pf.rules.warranty: 1 year on workmanship (the example's). Filled ground settles for weeks; that is not a defect, and the contract says what is covered.

pf.edges.weather: Heavy rain or high wind on a teardown day: the day moves, with no fee; the crew lead checks the forecast the day before
pf.edges.utility_not_off: A utility is not confirmed off: the work does not start; the start moves, with no fee
pf.edges.hazard_found: Asbestos, lead, an old oil tank or mold found: the work stops there; licensed removal first, by its own quote; a change order before more work
pf.edges.hidden_conditions: A second slab layer, a buried line or a hidden room found during the teardown: a change order before the fix
pf.edges.disposal_closed: The disposal site is closed or full: the haul-off moves a day, with no fee
pf.edges.permit_late: The start moves with no fee; Alex is told
pf.edges.inspection_fails: The crew fixes it and it's checked again; the last bill waits
pf.edges.cancel_after_window: Sam and the customer settle it; Rosie moves no money on its own
pf.edges.nobody_home: Teardown days with the gate open and the building empty, with start and end photos
pf.edges.over_license_limit: Not offered, and the owner is told why
pf.edges.walk_through_dispute: Goes to Sam; the last bill waits
pf.edges.other: All other edge cases are handled the generic way

notes:
Started from contractor (pattern: project; refitted that morning, not edited): an estimate visit, a written quote, then a contract and stage bills. Facts: documents, stages, photos, extrawork, firststeps, multiday, banktransfer, video; switch cancelright in flow B only (work sold at the customer's place); arrive A a set start, B a 2-hour window; cutoff 24 hours before.
Flow B main path visit|none|bill: the booking is the $89 estimate visit, credited to the job; Walt's written quote; the contract signed by everyone on the deed; $850 to start, $5,100 when the garage is down and the debris is hauled off, $2,550 at the finish (an $8,500 garage teardown). The $89 keeps the master's numbers true; a free estimate is the owner's choice (pf.money).
B money paths: visit|none|bill, visit|none|own, visit|card|bill, photos|deposit|bill (Shed teardown, $640 from photos, a $160 deposit, a $480 rest). Left out: list paths. Cleanout help ($179) and Debris pickup ($150) are in pf.services, but the master's booking cards name one list service, so a list path would show the wrong name (MASTER).
Flow A is Sam's second company, Lee Demo Office, a demolition planning office (the master's Lee's Barbershop). Main path list|card|counter: a $35 scope consult with Fern, a card saved for the $20 missed-consult fee, paid at the office desk. The other three: list|none|counter, list|full|none (teardown phasing session, $55, credited to the job if Alex signs), list|deposit|counter (demolition planning package, $140, $40 deposit).
Flow A can be a video or phone scope consult (fact `video`): the owner's photos and plans are enough to talk through a scope, so the A4-01 video branch is on.
Own steps: A8-x01 (the scope consult offers the estimate visit at home), B8-x06 to B8-x08 (the permit, the utility shut-offs and the asbestos and lead survey go first; a late permit moves the start with no fee; asbestos found means a licensed removal company first, by its own quote, and the start moves) and B8-x11 / B8-x12 (a second layer of concrete found under the slab: a change order first, signed by both).
Nothing comes down before the building is empty, every utility is confirmed off and capped, older buildings are tested for asbestos and lead where the rules require it, and the permit is in (pf.first_steps; B8-37's master 'Never' line on gas, water and power). A load-bearing wall needs an engineer's letter from the owner first (pf.services). Asbestos is removed only by a licensed removal company, never by this crew (pf.license lead_safe; own step B8-x08). Stop words: a gas smell or sparking wires; a wall, roof or floor falling or collapsing now, or someone trapped or hurt in a building. A storm-damaged building that is still standing, with nobody inside, is a go-on ('stay out').
Dates run forward: cancel window ends Tue Oct 27; permit, utilities and survey to-do Wed Oct 28 'due before the first work day, Mon Nov 2'; the survey result Thu Oct 29; a late permit Fri Oct 30 with new starts Mon Nov 9 / Mon Nov 16; the change order Tue Nov 3 (work days Mon Nov 2 to Wed Nov 4).
Booking choices: B timing settime, times window; A times setstart. Nothing is sent now (S2-30 'Yes' branch off, no `sentnow` fact), so nobody is on call. After turning it off, the joined text was searched for the opposite claim: S2-30's 'Neither demolition nor the office takes jobs sent now' and S1-21's 'Jobs sent now: None: every job is booked ahead' are re-worded; the other 'sent now' lines are the master's general rules for work that does send.
Plug-in splits kept whole (splitsKept): A7-15; B5-34, B7-55, B8-58, B8-69 (as the parent).
Self-checks: (1) the opposite-claim search above; (2) every example message was searched for this work's stop words (they appear only in the danger-words line and the plug-in); (3) B3-11 and B3-18 read as one Spanish conversation: the caller describes a go-on case, is asked about injury and gas, answers no, and gets the safety steps.
Names: Walt and Cruz are the crew leads (the master's Jordan and Casey), Fern and Asa the planners (Riley and Avery). None of them is a master customer's name. Addresses: 960 Depot Rd (the company), 45 Union St (the office), 18 Hawthorn Ct (Alex). License numbers use an obviously fake format (EX-1042, EX-2087, EX-3150, EX-4216, EX-5309), also in place of the master's S2-21 person licenses.
Every state rule is a switch from the state's form: the license and its job-size limit, the written contract and its parts, the deposit cap, money kept apart, the cancel window, permits, lien waivers, what must be shown. No state, city or number from one.
